issue_context.title: Error thrown from a hook is not propagating to custom error handler
comments:
Based on the [docs](https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Hooks/#the-onerror-hook) I believe this is intended:

> This hook is useful if you need to do some custom error logging or add some specific header in case of error.
It is not intended for changing the error, and calling reply.send will throw an exception.
I guess, the above is only for `onError` hook.

The error should be an instance of Error :)
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/7f274d1be8ed27e32662a29a5940194b602086e8/lib/reply.js#L98-L101

Thanks @delvedor. Got it.
But, if I throw from any place other than hook using this `throw { detail: "Token is not valid" }`  it is going to `errorHandler`. That's where my confusion started.

I think the confusion is something that we should address. IMHO it's either enabled somewhere or not. 

I _think_ we should only support throwing actual `Error` objects, however I see why developers tend to not do that. What do you think folks?

The custom error works only in `preSerialization` and `onSend` hooks for what I tested.
Maybe new tests should be added after the discussion.

I think that `Error` is less confusing for the reader and can be easily extended but, if ECMAScript admits it, we should support it. (checking the code it should not be painful, we already know if the handler has been rejected or not, we must provide that info to `reply.js`)

I think we should support it because [`throws`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/throw) accepts any kind of types, so the users expect correctly to manage an error throwing "something".

WDYT?

I don‘t know what you think about a change in semantics in order to support thrown plain objects, but for sure [there’s an error in the documentation](https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Reply/#async-await-and-promises) (emphasis in bold is mine):

> Rejected promises default to a `500` HTTP status code. Reject the promise, or `throw` in an `async function`, with ***an object that has `statusCode` (or `status`) and `message` properties*** to modify the reply.

The terms “an object” **does not** imply that an instance of _Error_ or of a subclass of _Error_ is required.

Made a PR to propose a docs improvement.
Just let me state that this issue got me too and I checked the docs twice to make sure I could send custom errors. Since I had a custom `HTTPError` class the solution for my case was as simple as `extend Error`.

Feature ready in v3
Stay tuned for the release!
